Welcome to the reference section for PHYC54H3 (Classical Mechanics). This section contains quick-reference articles covering the essential mathematical, physical, and computational tools used throughout the course.

### [Mathematical Identities & Calculus](math-identities-and-calculus.qmd)
A comprehensive cheatsheet of trigonometric identities, hyperbolic functions, essential derivatives, common integrals (including Gaussian integrals), and Taylor/Maclaurin series expansions.

### [Vector Calculus & Identities](vector-calculus-and-identities.qmd)
Formulas for dot and cross products, scalar and vector triple products (BAC-CAB), the Del operator ($\nabla$), divergence, gradient, curl, Laplacian, and the major integral theorems (Gauss's and Stokes's).

### [Physical Constants & Astronomical Data](physical-constants-and-data.qmd)
A reference table of fundamental physical constants (SI units), particle masses, solar system orbital and physical parameters, and common physics conversion factors.

### [Computational Methods for Mechanics](computational-methods.qmd)
An overview of the numerical integration techniques used to solve ODEs in classical mechanics, including the Euler method, 4th-Order Runge-Kutta (RK4), the symplectic Velocity Verlet method (critical for energy conservation in Hamiltonian systems), and SciPy's `solve_ivp`.
